evidence: Expected: malformed or schema-drifted Graph policy fields should be normalized safely or converted into a structured graph_error response, preserving the endpoint's documented error behavior.
Observed: normalize_policy assumes nested values such as conditions.users, applications, locations, grantControls, and sessionControls are dictionaries and calls .get on them without type checks.
An independent probe with {'id':'x','conditions':{'users':'bad'}} raised AttributeError at graph.py:161.

GraphClient.fetch_policies calls normalize_policy without translating normalization exceptions to GraphError, and server._policies catches only GraphError, so this path can terminate the request without a structured response.
findings.remediation: Validate each nested Graph object before accessing it, defaulting non-dictionaries to an empty dictionary or rejecting malformed policy payloads with GraphError("graph_error", ...). Ensure /api/policies returns a structured 502 rather than allowing an uncaught normalization exception.
findings.title: Malformed nested policy objects can crash /api/policies
findings.verification: Add mocked client tests for non-dictionary conditions/users/applications/locations/grantControls/sessionControls values and an endpoint-level test confirming malformed Graph data produces a structured response; rerun the full suite.
